method: After freezing the production pair, returned to the Biology annex tables and general regulations, then to the study guide assessment and registration requirements. Rebuilt the compulsory and choice-credit totals from those sources and reconsidered the current workbook course evidence and renderer mappings before confirming the finished record.
findings: For the standard September 2026 entry, seven compulsory 7.5 EC first-year courses and one of two restricted 7.5 EC electives make 60 EC. Academic Communication and the 15 EC graduation project take the compulsory total to 75 EC. The full restricted major basket is 60 EC, including the first-year choice, and requires at least 15 EC at level two and 30 EC at level three, including 22.5 EC from the starred subset. The remaining 45 EC are profiling, with at least 15 EC at levels two or three and no substantial course overlap. The full 180 EC outline preserves the official restricted basket without selecting a named track. The 11 study interests guide electives, and the former Molecular Life Sciences track ended on 31 August 2026.

The usual first-year BSA threshold is 45 EC, subject to formal exceptions and review of personal circumstances. Level-three Biology requires 15 EC of level-two major electives and applicable course-specific entry requirements, including animal practical preparation where specified. Time slots and exclusions for overlapping courses apply. After 165 EC, Biology elective placement is restricted while the project remains outstanding. Graduation project entry requires 120 Biology major EC including every compulsory first-year course and Academic Communication. The 15 EC project occupies both time slots in one period and combines supervised practical and literature research, a report and a presentation. The guide weights practical work, report and ownership at 50, 40 and 10 percent, respectively, and requires a pass in each. Optional Research PLUS is a separate elective. A minor, outside study or exchange can fit profiling subject to approvals and residency. The project’s entry and assessment requirements are embedded in the course credits.

The 52.5 EC of later major electives and the separate first-year elective are part of one 60 EC restricted requirement. The mandatory project is a separate 15 EC assessment combining supervised practical work and a literature report. It is excluded from the 120 EC threshold as the culminating component. Introductory biodiversity covers plant groups and microbes. Infection & Immunity provides a narrower microbial overlap with a host emphasis. Molecular Pathology & Genetics and the lab support genetic testing and DNA methods, alongside computational tools. Utrecht retains dedicated plant physiology and genomics. The broad, molecular and ecology options are materially different in disciplinary weight and meet the current offerings and formal prerequisites. The team project runs in term one, so it contributes early inquiry rather than final-year research. Optional independent research is represented separately in each option.
